 3  C.C.17281/2022  JUDGMENT
This is a private complaint registered by the complainant.
The matter has been referred to Nandini Police station U/s 156(3) of Cr.P.C.

On the basis of the complainant lodged by the complainant the Police Inspector, Nandini Layout P.S has registered the case and submitted the Charge Sheet against the accused No.1 to 4 or the offences punishable U/Secs.498(A), 323, 504 and 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
2.

The brief facts of the Prosecution case are as follows:
That the marriage of accused No.1 with C.W.1-Ms.Meena was solemnized on 12.12.2018 as per Hindu rites and customs and at the time of marriage the accused No.2 and 3 demanded and taken gold ornaments worth 200 grams for the bride and 80 grams gold ornaments for the bridegroom and cash of Rs.3,00,000/- as dowry and after marriage while C.W.1-Smt.Meena was residing with the accused No.1 to 4 at Meena vs Ranjith Kumar on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21436981/
2

the matrimonial home at Thiruvallur, the accused No.1 to 4 used to harass C.W.1 physically and mentally by demanding C.W.1 to get additional dowry of Rs.10 lakhs and used to abuse her and assaulted her with hands and shaving trimmer and sent her to her paternal house.

Further while C.W.1 was residing with her parents at No.47,
Teacher's colony, ShankarNag Nagar, Nandini Layout the accused No.1 used to come and physically and mentally harass C.W.1 in the matter of bringing additional dowry.

Thereby accused No.1 to 4 have committed the offences punishable U/Secs.498(A),
323, 504 and 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
3.

On the basis of the Statement of CW-1, the Nandini Layout Police have registered a case under Crime No.307/2021 for the offences punishable U/Secs.498(A), 323, 504 and 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act against the accused No.1 to 4 and submitted the FIR before the court.

Thereafter the investigating officer visited the spot and drawn the spot mahazar and recorded the statement of witnesses and on completion of the investigation, the Charge Sheet has been filed against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable U/Secs.498(A), 323, 504 and 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
On the receipt of police report this court has taken cognizance for the said offences.
4. On the appearance of the accused No.1 to 4 they were enlarged on bail.
The copies of prosecution papers were furnished to C.C.17281/2022 the accused as contemplated U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both the parties, the charge was framed against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable U/s 498A, 323, 324, 504 and 506 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act and read over to them.
The accused No.1 to 4 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Hence, the matter was posted for evidence.

5. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has got examined one witness as PW-1, out of total charge sheet witnesses as CW-1 to 12 and got marked two documents as Ex.P1 and P2.

Since PW-1 who is the material witness, has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution and the presence of rest of the material witnesses could not be secured and since there is no incriminating evidence against the accused No.1 to 4 from the material witnesses, no purpose would be served by issuing summons to rest of the witnesses.
Hence, the evidence of rest of the witnesses is dropped by rejecting the prayer of the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor.
The statement of the accused No.1 to 4 as required Under Sec.313(1)(b) of Cr.P.C was dispensed with as there was no incriminating circumstances in the evidence of prosecution witnesses.

6. I have heard the arguments addressed by the learned C.C.17281/2022 Assistant Public Prosecutor and learned advocate for the accused No.1 to 4.
7.

On going through the facts and circumstances of the prosecution case, the following points would arise for my consideration :

sentences.text: 1 . Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 married C.W.1- Ms.Meena on 12.12.2018 as per Hindu rites and customs and at the time of marriage the accused No.2 and 3 demanded and taken gold ornaments worth 200 grams for the bride and 80 grams gold ornaments for the bridegroom and cash of Rs.3,00,000/- as dowry and thereby the accused No.1 to 4 have committed the offence of "receiving and demanding dowry" punishable U/s 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage while C.W.1-Smt.Meena was residing with the accused No.1 to 4 at the matrimonial home the accused No.1 to 4 used to harass C.W.1 C.C.17281/2022 physically and mentally by demanding additional dowry of Rs.10,00,000/- and subjected C.W.1 to physical and mental harassment and sent her to her paternal house and thereby the accused No.1 to 4 have committed the offence of subjecting C.W.1 to cruelty,
punishable U/Sec. 498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was residing with the accused No.1 to 4 at Thiruvallur the accused No.1 to 4 picked up quarrel with C.W.1 in the matter of bringing additional dowry and abused C.W.1 in filthy language knowingly that it would give provocation to C.W.1 to breach public peace and thereby the accused No.1 to 4 have committed the offence of " intentional insult" punishable U/s 504 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was residing with the accused No.1 to 4 at Thiruvallur the accused No.1 to 4 picked up quarrel with C.W.1 in the matter of bringing additional dowry and the accused No.1 without any C.C.17281/2022 provocation assaulted C.W.1 with the shaving set and trimmer and caused hurt and thereby the accused No.1 has committed an offence punishable U/s 324 of IPC?
5. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was residing with the accused No.1 to 4 at the matrimonial house at Thiruvallur the accused No.1 picked up quarrel with C.W.1 in the matter of bringing additional dowry and the accused No.1 without any provocation assaulted C.W.1 with hands and caused hurt and thereby the accused No.1 to 4 have committed an offence punishable U/s 323 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
6. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was residing with accused at the matrimonial house, the accused No.1 to 4 used to criminally intimidate to the life of C.W.1 for forcing her to bring additional dowry and thereby the accused No.1 to 4 have committed an offence punishable U/s 506 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
7. What Order ?

My findings to the above Points are as under:
 Points No.1 to 6 : In the Negative.
Point No.7 :

As per final order,
 For the following: -
 REASONS  9.

Point No.1 to 6 :- As these points are inter linked with each other and also similar evidence is led on all these points, I have taken all these points together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and discussion.

10. It is allegation that the accused No.1 to 4 have committed the offences punishable U/Secs.498(A), 323, 504, 324, 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
11.
In order to prove its case, prosecution has got examined informant of crime/C.W.1 by name Smt.Meena as P.W.1.
Out of the documents marked for the prosecution Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar.
12. In support of the case of prosecution the informant of crime C.W1 is examined as P.W.1.
P.W.1 in her evidence has deposed that accused No.1 is her husband and accused No.2 and 3 are the father C.C.17281/2022 and mother of accused No.1, accused No.4 is the sister of accused No.1.
The accused persons have not demanded any dowry prior to marriage or after marriage and her parents have not given dowry to accused persons.
The accused persons have not extended physical and mental cruelty towards her.
She has further deposed that she has not lodged a complaint against the accused .
She does not know the contents of Ex.P.1- Complaint and Ex.P.2-Mahazar.
The police have not drawn mahazar in her presence.
13. The P.W.1 being the prime witness turned fully hostile to the case of prosecution.

In the lengthy cross examination of PW.1 made by learned Sr.A.P.P, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth to support the case of the prosecution and she deposed that she has compromised the matter with the accused persons.
14. Now on over all perusal of the evidence and prosecution witness, the complainant/PW-1 is the material witness has not supported the case of prosecution.

The PW-1 during the course of her evidence has not at all stated in respect of dowry harassment by the accused No.1 to 4 and she has denied the involvement of the C.C.17281/2022 accused No.1 to 4 and at the out set she has denied the entire case of the prosecution.

However, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor prays to issue Meena vs Ranjith Kumar on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21436981/
5 summon to other witnesses.

Having considered the facts and circumstances of this case, this court was of the opinion that even if other witnesses were examined, it would be a futile exercise and no lawful purpose would have been served.

As such examination of the prosecution witnesses only for the purpose of completing the procedural aspect and will not serve any judicial purpose and it is sheer waste of the precious time of the court.
Therefore, the prayer of the learned APP to issue summons to other witnesses was rejected.

At this stage this court relied upon judgment delivered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1996 (3) Crimes 84 Sathish Mehra V/s Delhi Administration &
another:

entities.text: 1996 (3) Crimes 84 Sathish Mehra V/s Delhi Administration
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
wherein at page No.13 the Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date".
The principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above case is applicable in this case also.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution C.C.17281/2022 has failed to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 to 4 beyond all reasonable doubts.

Under these facts and circumstances of the case, the above Point No.1 to 6 are answered in the 'NEGATIVE'.
15.
Point No7:

- In view of the findings of point No.1 to 6, this court proceed to pass the following;
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of Cr.P.C. accused No.1 to 4 are acquitted of the offences punishable U/Secs.498(A), 323, 324, 504, 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
Bail bonds of the accused No.1 and 2 and Surety bonds shall stand canceled.
The bail bond executed under Section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. shall be continued.
